title: Payment of a Deceased Employee's Wages to a Surviving Spouse Without Probate — Information Sheet

title: Director's Inspection Rights — Information Sheet
description: Explains Cal. Corp. Code § 1602, a California corporate director's own statutory right to inspect and copy the corporation's books, records, and documents and to inspect its physical properties — distinct from the shareholder's inspection right documented in this corpus's Shareholder and Member Inspection Rights information sheet. Covers the statute's own "absolute right" wording and its broader-than-shareholder scope, the absence of any stated-purpose condition (unlike the shareholder's right), inspection by agent or attorney, and the court remedy for a refused inspection demand — with an honest disclosure that applying that remedy to a refused director demand is a structural reading of the statute's placement and wording, not an express cross-reference.

title: Preliminary and Final Declarations of Disclosure — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's mandatory financial-disclosure framework in a dissolution, legal-separation, or nullity proceeding, Family Code §§ 2100-2113 — the general framework this corpus's Bifurcation of Marital Status document explicitly flagged as not yet independently covered. Covers the Legislature's stated purpose and each party's continuing duty to update disclosure, the requirement of two separate sequential disclosures (preliminary and final), the preliminary declaration's required content and service deadlines, the final declaration's required content, timing, and mutual-waiver mechanism with its five required representations, and the mandatory monetary-sanctions and judgment-set-aside consequences for noncompliance.

title: LLC Member Dissociation and Buyout — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act default rules on member dissociation, Corp. Code §§ 17706.01-17706.03, 17707.01, 17707.03 — a genuine companion to this corpus's Partnership Agreement document, which covers dissociation under a separate statute (the 1994 Uniform Partnership Act) for general partnerships, not LLCs. Covers the statutory events that dissociate a member, the distinction between the power to dissociate (which always exists) and wrongful dissociation (which carries liability), the default effect of dissociation on voting/management/economic rights, why dissociation does not itself dissolve the LLC, and — a key finding — the absence of any general statutory buyout right for an ordinarily dissociated member, apart from a narrower mechanism tied specifically to avoiding a judicial dissolution decree.

title: California Invasion of Privacy Act (CIPA) — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Invasion of Privacy Act, Penal Code §§ 630-638.55 — a distinct body of law from this corpus's employee-monitoring content, which addresses employer computer/email/network systems specifically. CIPA governs the recording, wiretapping, and interception of communications broadly, regardless of an employment relationship, and carries both criminal penalties and a private civil right of action. Covers the wiretapping/unauthorized-connection prohibition (§ 631), the all-party consent requirement for recording a confidential communication (§ 632) and the statute's own definitions, the evidentiary exclusion rule both sections state for unlawfully obtained material, and the private right of action's statutory damages and injunctive relief (§ 637.2).

title: Employee Political Activity Protection — Information Sheet
description: Explains California Labor Code §§ 1101-1106, which protect employees' political activities and affiliations — a genuine, standalone topic only incidentally cross-referenced elsewhere in this corpus (as an exception carve-out in wage-retaliation citations), not substantively covered until now. Covers the core prohibition on employer rules restricting political activity, the separate prohibition on coercing employees through threat of discharge, the California Supreme Court's construction of "political activity" as not narrowly confined to partisan activity, and the chapter's own criminal misdemeanor penalty and preserved civil damages remedy.

title: Restriction on Requiring Arbitration as a Condition of Employment — Information Sheet
description: Explains California Labor Code § 432.6 (AB 51), which restricts requiring arbitration as a condition of employment — a companion to this corpus's Arbitration Agreement drafting template, addressing the separate statutory restriction rather than the agreement's own terms. Covers the statute's own prohibition and its FAA-enforceable-agreement savings clause, and — critically — its current, court-ordered enforcement status: the Ninth Circuit's 2023 holding in Chamber of Commerce v. Bonta that the FAA preempts the statute as applied to arbitration agreements, and the resulting January 2024 permanent injunction barring named California officials from enforcing § 432.6(a)-(c) wherever the alleged waiver is an FAA-covered arbitration agreement.

title: Wage-and-Hour Claim Filing Deadlines — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's general civil statutes of limitations as applied to wage-and-hour claims after employment ends — a companion to this corpus's DLSE Wage Claim and Waiting-Time Penalty Demand documents, resolving a nuanced point those documents' own clauses flagged as unverified. Covers the three-year deadline for a statutory wage claim (confirmed for both unpaid final wages and meal/rest period premium pay), the four-year deadline for a claim founded on a written contract, why the Labor Code § 203 waiting-time penalty's filing deadline tracks the underlying wage claim's own period rather than the general one-year penalty deadline — confirmed by California Supreme Court authority (Pineda v. Bank of America) even where the penalty is sued for alone — and the absence of a separate filing deadline in the statute authorizing a DLSE administrative wage claim.

title: Water-Conserving Plumbing Fixture Compliance Disclosure — Information Sheet
description: Explains Civil Code §§ 1101.1-1101.9, California's water-conserving plumbing fixture retrofit and disclosure requirement for pre-1994 residential and commercial real property — a separate statutory scheme (Civil Code) from this corpus's Smoke Alarm and CO Device Compliance Disclosure document (Health & Safety Code). Covers the statute's own defined terms ("noncompliant plumbing fixture," "water-conserving plumbing fixture"), the single-family retrofit deadline (January 1, 2017) and seller's disclosure duty, the later multifamily/commercial deadline (January 1, 2019) and its own disclosure duty, and the statute's exemption list — narrower and differently drawn than the smoke alarm statute's exemptions.

title: California Recording Act and Priority of Interests — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's real property recording system, Civil Code §§ 1213, 1214, 1217 — deepening two supporting clauses already embedded in this corpus's Grant Deed/Quitclaim Deed and Living Trust Funding documents into a dedicated, standalone explainer that adds genuinely new depth: the recording-and-indexing requirement for constructive notice, and California case law construing "good faith" and "notice" for purposes of the race-notice priority rule. Covers the core priority rule (§ 1214) and its three-part race-notice structure, what recording actually accomplishes and the indexing requirement courts have added to it (§ 1213), an unrecorded instrument's continued validity between the original parties (§ 1217), and how courts have defined "good faith" and "notice" (actual vs. constructive, the reasonable-inquiry standard).

title: IAEA Notice of Proposed Action Procedure — Information Sheet
description: Explains the Notice of Proposed Action procedure under California's Independent Administration of Estates Act, Probate Code §§ 10580-10592 — deepening a gap the corpus's own Petition for Probate document explicitly flagged as not independently researched. Covers when notice is required versus optional, who must receive it and how written consent or waiver eliminates the requirement, the notice's required content and delivery timing/method under Probate Code § 1215 (including that the 15-day period is not extended for mail or electronic delivery), how a person objects and the ex parte restraining-order alternative, what happens after a timely objection versus silence, and the noncompliance consequences — third-party/bona fide purchaser protection and the court's discretionary authority to remove the personal representative.

title: Ademption and Abatement of Testamentary Gifts — Information Sheet
description: Explains two related California statutory doctrines determining what a beneficiary actually receives from an estate: ademption (Probate Code §§ 21133-21140), covering what happens to a specific gift when the specifically-given property is no longer part of the estate at death, and abatement (Probate Code §§ 21400-21406), covering the statutory order in which gifts are reduced when the estate's assets are insufficient. A companion to this corpus's Last Will and Testament and Grounds to Contest a Will/Trust documents, neither of which addresses these doctrines. Covers ademption by extinction and its statutory substitute rights, the incapacity exception for sales/encumbrances by a conservator, agent, or trustee, ademption by satisfaction's four-condition test, the precise six-class statutory abatement order and a testator's power to override it, and the pro-rata-within-class and exoneration rules.

title: Domestic Worker Bill of Rights — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Domestic Worker Bill of Rights, Labor Code §§ 1450-1455, which extended overtime protections to personal attendants (in-home caregivers, largely excluded from general overtime rules before this law) — only incidentally referenced elsewhere in this corpus as an exemption category, not substantively covered until now. Covers the statute's coverage of "domestic work" and its exclusions, the definition of "personal attendant" and its 20%-other-work ceiling, domestic work employee status and statutory exclusions (family members, IHSS workers, casual babysitters), and the distinct overtime formula for personal attendants (1.5x after 9 hours/day or 45 hours/week, verified as different from the general 8-hour/40-hour standard).

title: California Genetic Information Privacy Act — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Genetic Information Privacy Act, Civil Code § 56.18 et seq. — a state consumer-privacy statute governing direct-to-consumer genetic testing companies' data practices, distinct from this corpus's GINA document (a federal employment-discrimination statute). Covers who the statute regulates and its "express consent" definition, the required privacy-practices summary and notice, the statute's five-category menu of separate consents (not one blanket consent), the revocation/sample-destruction/data-security/access-deletion mechanisms, the nondiscrimination rule and the restriction on disclosure to insurers and employers, and the enforcement structure — civil penalties prosecuted exclusively by named public officials, explicitly not a standalone private right of action.

title: California Talent Agencies Act — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Talent Agencies Act, Labor Code § 1700 et seq., which regulates who may lawfully procure employment or engagements for an artist and requires licensing by the Labor Commissioner. Covers the statutory definition of "talent agency" and "artists," the recording-contract carve-out, the licensing requirement, the required Labor-Commissioner-approved contract form and disclosure, the Labor Commissioner's role in hearing controversies (including that unlicensed activity is not itself a criminal act, and the one-year time limit), and Marathon Entertainment, Inc. v. Blasi's holding that the Act applies to personal managers who procure employment, with the Labor Commissioner's discretion to sever rather than void an entire contract.

title: Severance Pay — Is It Required? Information Sheet
description: Explains what California law does and does not require regarding severance pay at the end of employment: the absence of a general default entitlement to severance, how an employer's own voluntary severance promise can become a binding unilateral contract once made, and how this differs from the California WARN Act's separate notice-failure liability (Labor Code § 1402).

title: Section 2641 Reimbursement for Community Contributions to Education or Training — Information Sheet
description: Explains California Family Code section 2641's community-reimbursement right when community or quasi-community property paid for a party's education or training that substantially enhanced that party's earning capacity — the core right, the interest and loan-assignment rules, the statutory reduction grounds including the ten-year rebuttable presumption, and the exclusive-remedy and written-agreement-waiver provisions. A distinct statute from Family Code section 2640, covered in a separate companion information sheet.

title: Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children (ICPC) — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's enactment of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children (Family Code §§ 7900-7913), which governs placing a child across state lines for foster care or as a preliminary to a possible adoption: the compact's stated purpose, what counts as a covered "placement" and a statutory exclusion for certain relative placements, the pre-placement notice-and-approval requirement, the sending agency's continuing jurisdiction, and the California agency designated to administer compact notices.

description: Explains the IWC Wage Orders' provide-and-maintain duty for a required employee uniform: the Wage Order's own definition of "uniform" (distinctive design or color, not an employee's ordinary basic wardrobe), which industries and occupations the requirement was confirmed to cover, and the exemptions for administrative/executive/professional employees and (with limited exceptions) public employees. title: California Age-Appropriate Design Code Act — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Age-Appropriate Design Code Act (Civil Code § 1798.99.28 et seq.): the statute's own "likely to be accessed by children" coverage test, its core codified duties (Data Protection Impact Assessment, age estimation, default privacy settings), its data-use and dark-patterns restrictions, and its Attorney-General-exclusive enforcement scheme with no private right of action. Also traces the ongoing NetChoice, LLC v. Bonta litigation and states, as of the most recent ruling reviewed, which provisions are currently enjoined (the DPIA requirement, the notice-and-cure provision, and the data-use/dark-patterns restrictions on vagueness grounds) and which are not (the coverage definition and age estimation requirement) — a preliminary-injunction posture, not a final judgment.

title: Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act — Information Sheet

A separate, older statute from this project's AB 1482 (statewide Tenant Protection Act) document, which works by a different mechanism.

title: Good Neighbor Fence Act — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Good Neighbor Fence Act (Civil Code § 841): the presumption that adjoining landowners share equally in the reasonable costs of a boundary fence's construction, maintenance, or replacement, the 30-day written notice a landowner must give before incurring those costs and its required content, the statutory factors a court considers to rebut the presumption, and what the statute does and does not provide if the landowners disagree. A separate statute from this project's Boundary Line Agreement document, which covers the different question of where a disputed boundary line is located.

title: California ABC Test for Worker Classification — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's own statutory worker-classification test (Labor Code §§ 2775-2776, codifying Dynamex Operations West, Inc. v. Superior Court): the presumption of employee status and the hiring entity's burden, the three required ABC factors, the test's own stated scope and its fallback to the older Borello multi-factor test, and the business-to-business exemption. title: California "Eraser Law" (Minor's Right to Remove Posted Content) — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's Eraser Law (Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 22580-22582): the dual coverage trigger (an operator directed to minors OR one with actual knowledge a minor is a user), the core removal right limited to content the minor registered user posted themselves (not a broad right to be forgotten), the required notice and instructions, and the statute's own exceptions and "deemed compliant" safe harbor — invisibility to other users and the public, not guaranteed deletion from the operator's servers.

title: California Warehouse Quota Law — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's warehouse quota law (Labor Code §§ 2100-2112, AB 701): the employee-count and NAICS-code coverage threshold for a "warehouse distribution center employer," the written quota disclosure requirement, the prohibition on a quota that prevents meal/rest compliance or bathroom use, the employee's conditional right to request quota and personal work-speed data, and the rebuttable presumption of retaliation.

title: PAGA Representative Claims and Arbitration — Information Sheet
description: Explains the current, combined effect of Viking River Cruises, Inc. v. Moriana (2022) and Adolph v. Uber Technologies, Inc. (2023) on whether an arbitration agreement can compel arbitration of an employee's individual PAGA claim while the representative portion proceeds in court: the FAA preempts California's Iskanian rule against splitting PAGA claims, but the California Supreme Court held in Adolph that compelling arbitration of the individual claim does not, by itself, strip the employee of standing to pursue the non-individual claims in court. Distinct from this project's PAGA Pre-Suit Notice Letter document, which covers pre-suit notice mechanics.

title: UCC-1 Financing Statement — Information and Filing Worksheet
description: Explains California Commercial Code Division 9's rules for perfecting a security interest in personal property by filing a UCC-1 financing statement: the statutory sufficiency requirements, the distinction between a security interest's attachment and its perfection, who must authorize the filing, the financing statement's five-year duration and the consequences of lapse, and the general first-in-time priority rule filing accomplishes.

title: Split Shift Premium Pay — Additional Requirements Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the Wage Order's own text, additional facts about California's split shift premium pay requirement beyond the core one-hour premium formula and live-in-employee exception already covered in this project's Reporting Time Pay Information Sheet: the IWC Wage Order's formal definition of a 'split shift,' DLSE's stated enforcement position on how long an unpaid interruption must last before it is treated as a split shift rather than a bona fide meal or rest period, and the Wage Order's separate recordkeeping duty for split shift intervals.

title: Structural Pest Control Inspection Report — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statutes' own text, California's structural pest control ('wood destroying pests or organisms') inspection report requirements: the Civil Code § 1099 delivery trigger (conditional on certification/report being a condition of the contract or financing, not universal), the Business and Professions Code § 8516 licensing and 10-business-day timing requirements, the statute's own distinction between evident infestation and conditions likely to lead to infestation, the § 8519 optional certification and its statutory 'no infestation' text, and the § 8517/§ 8518 requirements that later correspondence reference the report and that completed work be noticed.

title: California Uniform Directed Trust Act ('Trust Director' / 'Trust Protector') — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statute's own text, California's Uniform Directed Trust Act (Prob. Code §§ 16600-16632, effective January 1, 2024), which governs a person who holds authority over some aspect of a trust's administration without serving as trustee -- a role sometimes called a 'trust protector' in general estate-planning practice, though the statute's own text uses only 'trust director' and 'power of direction.' Covers the statutory definitions, the scope of a 'power of direction' and what it expressly excludes (including the power to appoint or remove a trustee), the trust director's default fiduciary status, how a directed trustee must respond to a trust director's exercise of power, and the default procedural rules (acceptance, bond, compensation, resignation, vacancy) and applicability date.

title: California Uniform Simultaneous Death Act — General Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statute's own text, California's general Uniform Simultaneous Death Act default rule (Prob. Code § 220) for when priority of death cannot be established, and its more specific applications: gifts conditioned on survivorship generally (§ 222), joint tenancy division into equal shares (§ 223), and community/quasi-community property division (§ 103). Also explains how § 221(a) confirms these are genuinely distinct, separately-triggered provisions rather than restatements of one another -- and cross-references, rather than restates, this corpus's existing will-beneficiary (120-hour rule) and life-insurance-beneficiary simultaneous-death clauses.

title: Fraudulent Inducement to Change Residence for Work (Labor Code §§ 970-972) — Information Sheet

title: Notice to an Alleged Father in an Adoption Proceeding — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statutes' own text, California's process for identifying and giving notice to an alleged father in an adoption proceeding under Family Code §§ 7660-7671. Corrects a common assumption: unlike a number of other states, California does not maintain a centralized, self-registration 'putative father registry.' Instead, the court and a state or county agency (the State Department of Social Services, per § 7663(a)(1)) have an affirmative duty to search for and identify an alleged father, then serve him actual notice with a 30-day statutory response window. Covers the mandatory inquiry, notice and the 30-day deadline, the alleged father's own voluntary waiver/denial mechanism, and what happens when no alleged father can be identified at all, including the 45-day hearing deadline.

title: Noncompete Void Notification (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600.1(b)) — Information Sheet and Notice Template
description: Explains, using the statute's own text, the employer's affirmative duty under Business and Professions Code § 16600.1(b) to notify current employees, and former employees employed after January 1, 2022, whose contract includes a void noncompete clause, that the clause is void -- a duty separate from the general noncompete prohibition already covered in this project's Non-Compete Agreement document. Covers the notice deadline, the required written, individualized, dual-channel delivery, and the statute's own unfair-competition enforcement consequence, and includes a notice template.

title: Motion Picture and Broadcasting Industry Final-Wage Timing (Labor Code § 201.5) — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statute's own text, California's distinct final-wage timing rule for employees engaged in the production or broadcasting of motion pictures (Labor Code § 201.5): the statute's own two-part definition of covered work and workers, the next-regular-payday due date (a different trigger from the general immediate-on-discharge and 72-hour-on-quit rules), the mailing/on-site-availability payment option, the broad definition of 'terminates' (covering resignation and specified-term expiration, not just discharge), the collective bargaining agreement carve-out, and the Section 203 waiting-time penalty cross-reference.

title: Restrictions on Employer Inquiry Into Arrest, Diversion, and Sealed Conviction Records (Labor Code § 432.7) — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statutes' own text, California Labor Code § 432.7's restrictions on an employer asking about, seeking, or using an applicant's or employee's arrest not resulting in conviction, diversion program participation, or a judicially dismissed or sealed conviction, plus § 432.8's separate extension of those limitations to certain marijuana-related convictions more than two years old. Covers the core prohibition, the statutory definition of 'conviction,' the stated exceptions (peace officers/criminal justice agencies, the 'particular conviction' exceptions, and legally-required background checks), and the civil/criminal remedies. Deepens what this project's Fair Chance Act document only cross-references without independently verifying.

title: California Pregnancy Disability Leave Law (Gov. Code § 12945) — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statutes' own text, California's pregnancy disability leave law (Gov. Code § 12945), part of FEHA: the core leave entitlement (up to four months, tied to actual disability duration, not a flat grant), the covered-employer threshold via § 12926's cross-referenced definition, group health plan coverage during leave, the prohibition on interference with the right, and how this leave relates to -- and is additive with -- CFRA and FMLA leave. Distinct from this project's CFRA document (family-care/bonding leave), Pregnant Workers Fairness Act document (a federal reasonable-accommodation duty), and Paid Family Leave document (a wage-replacement benefit, not job-protected leave itself).

title: Death-on-Property and HIV/AIDS-Status Disclosure ('Stigmatized Property,' Civ. Code § 1710.2) — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statute's own text, California Civil Code § 1710.2's disclosure rules for real property sale, lease, or rental transactions: the three-year no-duty-to-disclose rule for an occupant's death or its manner (with no cause of action arising from non-disclosure), the separate, time-unlimited no-duty rule for a prior occupant's HIV/AIDS status, and the Legislature's stated intent to occupy the field on both subjects. Also covers the statute's own express limits: it does not alter other physical/mental-condition disclosure duties, and does not immunize an intentional misrepresentation made in response to a direct inquiry about deaths on the property.

title: California Intestate Succession Distribution Shares (Prob. Code §§ 6400-6402) — Information Sheet
description: Explains, using the statutes' own text, California's default statutory scheme for dividing a decedent's property when there is no valid will covering all or part of the estate: the § 6400 trigger, the surviving spouse's or registered domestic partner's separate-property share on a sliding scale (entire estate, one-half, or one-third depending on which relatives survive -- distinct from the spouse's community/quasi-community property share already covered elsewhere in this corpus), and § 6402's full descent order when there is no surviving spouse or partner (descendants, then parents, then siblings' issue, then grandparents and their issue, then issue of a predeceased spouse, then next of kin generally, then in-laws of a predeceased spouse). Distinct from this project's Petition for Probate document, which covers who is APPOINTED administrator (§§ 8460-8461), a different question from who INHERITS.

title: Presumption of Fraud or Undue Influence — Donative Transfers to a Disqualified Person — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's statutory presumption of fraud or undue influence for a donative transfer to a "disqualified person" under Probate Code sections 21380, 21382, and 21384, and Evidence Code section 606: the seven categories of disqualified person (the instrument's drafter, a fiduciary who transcribed it, certain care custodians of a dependent adult, and their relatives, cohabitants, employees, and law-firm associates), the rebuttable-versus-conclusive split in who bears which presumption and the clear-and-convincing-evidence standard, the cost-shifting rule for an unsuccessful rebuttal, the statutory exceptions (including the asymmetric fourth-degree blood/affinity exemption and the small-transfer exemption), and the Certificate of Independent Review escape route. Distinct from the corpus's existing Omitted Spouse, Elder/Dependent Adult Financial Abuse, and Grounds to Contest a Will or Trust documents.

title: Accessory Dwelling Unit / Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit Ministerial Approval — Information Sheet
description: Explains California's ministerial local-agency approval process for accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and junior accessory dwelling units (JADUs) under Government Code Chapter 13, sections 66310-66342 (recodified from former sections 65852.2 and 65852.22 by SB 477, effective March 25, 2024, and further amended by 2025 legislation effective January 1, 2026): the ministerial-review mandate and completeness/approval/appeal timelines, the statutory floors and ceilings a local ordinance's lot-size, unit-size, and height standards must respect, the circumstances in which no parking requirement may be imposed and the one-space cap when it can be, the rule that no owner-occupancy requirement may be imposed on an ADU as such, and the JADU's distinct size cap and conditional owner-occupancy rule tied to shared sanitation facilities. Distinct from the corpus's existing Home Improvement Contract document and the ADU cross-references inside the AB 1482 rent-cap/just-cause exemption clauses.
